page: Microsoft Azure E4ads_v6 is a memory-optimized virtual machine belonging to the Eadv6 server family. It is powered by an AMD EPYC 9V74 processor utilizing the x86_64 architecture, running on the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor. The instance features 4 dedicated vCPUs derived from 2 physical cores with multithreading enabled. Memory capacity is 32.0 GB, yielding a high memory-to-vCPU ratio of 8.0 GB per core. Local storage is provided via a bundled 236 GB NVMe SSD, and the instance is Premium Storage capable. No GPU accelerators or complimentary public IPv4 addresses are included.

Performance benchmarks reveal a contrast between single-core and multi-core capabilities. The server demonstrates strong single-core CPU performance, scoring in the top 25% on stress-ng single-core and Geekbench single-core tests, alongside strong text processing. However, multi-core CPU performance, PassMark CPU scores, and Redis SET operations fall into the average range. Tradeoffs are evident in memory bandwidth, where read-only small and large block operations score in the bottom 25%, though write operations remain average. Database operations and software compilation also rank in the weak category.

From a cost-efficiency perspective, the E4ads_v6 offers high memory density per vCPU, making it a viable option for memory-bound workloads that do not require extreme memory read speeds. Given the strong single-core execution and average multi-core scaling, this server is appropriate for memory-intensive applications, caching layers, light web serving, and basic text processing tasks. It is less suitable for heavy database operations or large-scale multi-threaded compilation due to its weaker memory read bandwidth and database benchmark results.
